did_you_know.text: Did you know? At the entrance to the temple, two pillars were measured, each six cubits wide; together they formed the width of the vestibule.
Did you know? The entrance to the temple was ten cubits wide, while the temple was forty cubits long and twenty cubits wide.
Did you know? The inner room was twenty cubits by twenty cubits, and the man measuring it identified it as the Most Holy Place.
Did you know? The wall of the temple was six cubits thick, and the width of the side chambers surrounding it was four cubits.
Did you know? Around the temple were side chambers arranged in thirty-three levels, attached to the wall without penetrating it.
Did you know? The side chambers became wider toward the top because the structure of the temple grew wider at the upper levels.
Did you know? Between the chambers surrounding the temple was an area twenty cubits wide, encircling the temple on every side.
Did you know? Behind the temple area, on the western side, stood a building seventy cubits wide, with walls five cubits thick and a length of ninety cubits.
Did you know? The walls of the temple were decorated with cherubim and palm trees, with a palm tree placed between each cherub.
Did you know? Each cherub had two faces: a human face on one side and a young lion’s face on the other, and the decorations continued around the temple.
Did you know? Inside the temple stood a wooden altar, three cubits high and two cubits long; the prophet heard that it was the table that stood before the Lord.
Did you know? The temple and the sanctuary had double doors, and each door had two panels that swung open.
